newsitem.title: FRANCE: France raises CSG tax, cuts payroll charges.
newsitem.headline: France raises CSG tax, cuts payroll charges.

text.p: The French government said on Thursday that it was raising the CSG tax, a flat tax on most income, to 3.4 percent from 2.4 percent.
The new CSG (Generalised Social Contribution), used to fund welfare spending, will also be widened to cover virtually all income, including savings.
It said it was cutting 1.3 percentage points off payroll charges used to fund healthcare.
Altogether, it will raise seven billion francs in extra taxes to fund the welfare system.

It said in a statement that it was cutting income taxes next year by 25 billion francs, which once the additional welfare taxes were taken into account, would produce a net tax cut of 18 billion francs.
